newsitem.title: croatia: SOCCER-GLIHA HAT-TRICK EARNS DRAW FOR SLOVENIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GLIHA HAT-TRICK EARNS DRAW FOR SLOVENIA.

text.p: Primoz Gliha scored a hat-trick in only 21 minutes to give Slovenia a 3-3 draw with Croatia in a World Cup group one qualifier on Wednesday after the home side led 3-1 with 30 minutes to play.

Two goals from Zvonimir Boban after 43 and 60 minutes and one from Robert Prosinecki in the 33rd minute put Croatia in the driving seat, but Gliha's secured Slovenia's first point in four matches with his goals in the 45th, 65th and 67th minutes.
Slovenia also had a great chance to win the match in injury time when they broke for goal with the Croatian defence in tatters, but wasted the opportunity.
The result means that Croatia have now drawn their last three matches at home and remain third in the group behind Greece and Denmark.
Croatia were without five first choice regulars but looked to have done enough to win with two superbly taken goals by captain Boban as well as Prosinecki's opener.

But Gliha punished some poor defending by lobbing goalkeeper Tonci Gabric for the opener from long distance for the first and then grabbing two more from close range in two minutes midway through the second half.
"It was a match that happens once in a player's career," said Gliha, a former Zagreb player.
Croatian coach Miroslav Blazevic only said gloomily: "I can't believe this has happened."
Blazevic was forced to field a much changed side because of injuries and the suspension of leading scorer Davor Suker.
Despite that, Croatia looked in command for much of the match but were let down by defensive and goalkeeping errors.

"Croatia were handed two clumsy goals that significantly diminished our chances of qualifying for France," Blazevic's assistant Branko Ivankovic said. "But not everything is lost. We will play against Greece with a much stronger team. We have to win."
